page: Google Cloud Platform n2-standard-2 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance configured with 2 vCPUs and 8 GB of system memory. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it features a dedicated Intel Xeon processor running at 2.8 GHz, consisting of 1 physical core and 2 threads per core. The CPU cache configuration includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 33 MB of L3 cache. This instance does not include bundled local storage or GPU accelerators, and it comes with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations indicate that the n2-standard-2 operates in the lower performance tiers for most compute and memory tasks. It registers a stress-ng single-core score of 1398.19 and a multi-core score of 1837.38. Memory bandwidth is also limited, with read-only large block speeds at 13.8 GB/sec and write speeds at 11.79 GB/sec. While single-threaded gzip compression achieves an average throughput of 23.81 GB/sec, other metrics like the Geekbench multi-core score of 1333.0 and Passmark database operations score of 731.04 fall into the bottom 10% of tested hardware.

The primary tradeoff of the n2-standard-2 is its low resource density and modest processing throughput, which restricts its utility for resource-intensive applications. From a cost efficiency perspective, it serves as an entry-level option for workloads that require dedicated CPU allocation but do not demand high memory bandwidth or parallel processing power. It is best suited for lightweight general-purpose tasks, basic web serving, simple text processing, and small-scale development or testing environments.
